name: Auckland Central
boundary_note: The boundaries of Auckland Central, Mt Albert and Epsom move in a roughly anticlockwise direction, while Tāmaki and Maungakiekie move eastwards and Mt Roskill moves westwards.

name: Banks Peninsula
boundary_note: All these electorates remain unchanged from their 2020 boundaries and names.

name: Botany
boundary_note: Papakura moves southwards and shifts rural population to Botany, which in turn shifts some urban population to Pakuranga.

name: Christchurch Central
boundary_note: Through the hearings process, we adopted an alternate proposal that kept Redwood within Christchurch Central and instead moved a section in Linwood/Phillipstown between Fitzgerald Avenue, Avonside Drive, and Tuam Street into Christchurch East.

name: Christchurch East
boundary_note: Through the hearings process, we adopted an alternate proposal that kept Redwood within Christchurch Central and instead moved a section in Linwood/Phillipstown between Fitzgerald Avenue, Avonside Drive, and Tuam Street into Christchurch East.

name: Coromandel
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.

name: Dunedin
boundary_note: All these electorates remain unchanged from their 2020 boundaries and names.

name: East Cape
boundary_note: East Coast becomes East Cape.

name: East Coast Bays
boundary_note: Upper Harbour, which must lose population, experiences significant changes in addition to those mentioned above, shifting two areas to Henderson and East Coast Bays.

name: Epsom
boundary_note: The boundaries of Auckland Central, Mt Albert and Epsom move in a roughly anticlockwise direction, while Tāmaki and Maungakiekie move eastwards and Mt Roskill moves westwards.

name: Glendene
boundary_note: Parts of Kelston and Te Atatū become Glendene.

name: Hamilton East
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.

name: Hamilton West
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.

name: Henderson
boundary_note: Parts of Te Atatū, Upper Harbour and Kaipara ki Mahurangi become Henderson.

name: Hutt South
boundary_note: Hutt South and Remutaka both shift south-westwards, with the former taking in eastern Newlands.

name: Ilam
boundary_note: This in turn necessitated flow-on changes to Christchurch Central, Christchurch East and Ilam, to ensure they remained within quota.

name: Invercargill
boundary_note: Our proposed changes involved a population of around 900 in the vicinity of Nightcaps and Otautau moving from Southland to Invercargill.

name: Kaikōura
boundary_note: The Commission did receive a small number of submissions from West Coast-Tasman and Kaikōura, however we have been unable to accommodate these suggestions due to population quota requirements, and they remain unchanged from 2020 boundaries and names.

name: Kaipara ki Mahurangi
boundary_note: Kaipara ki Mahurangi shifts population to Upper Harbour and Henderson, while gaining an area from Whangaparāoa, which in turn shifts population to East Coast Bays.

name: Kapiti
boundary_note: Parts of Ōtaki and Mana become Kapiti.

name: Kenepuru
boundary_note: Parts of Mana and Ōhāriu become Kenepuru.

name: Māngere
boundary_note: There are also changes on the eastern boundaries of both Māngere and Manurewa.

name: Manurewa
boundary_note: There are also changes on the eastern boundaries of both Māngere and Manurewa.

name: Maungakiekie
boundary_note: The boundaries of Auckland Central, Mt Albert and Epsom move in a roughly anticlockwise direction, while Tāmaki and Maungakiekie move eastwards and Mt Roskill moves westwards.

name: Mt Albert
boundary_note: To ensure Mt Albert remains within quota, an area around Arch Hill is shifted from Auckland Central to Mt Albert.

name: Mt Maunganui
boundary_note: Parts of Bay of Plenty and Tauranga become Mt Maunganui.

name: Mt Roskill
boundary_note: The boundaries of Auckland Central, Mt Albert and Epsom move in a roughly anticlockwise direction, while Tāmaki and Maungakiekie move eastwards and Mt Roskill moves westwards.

name: Napier
boundary_note: Instead, Napier gains a rural area from Tukituki north of the Ngaruroro River.

name: Nelson
boundary_note: All these electorates remain unchanged from their 2020 boundaries and names.

name: New Plymouth
boundary_note: New Plymouth gains a small area east of the Waitara River from Taranaki-King Country, so Waitara township is now wholly within New Plymouth instead of being split between the two electorates.

name: North Shore
boundary_note: East Coast Bays also shifts small areas to both Upper Harbour and North Shore.

name: Northcote
boundary_note: Northcote and North Shore both expand northward in small areas, while Kaipara ki Mahurangi expands into a small area south of Coatesville, which is moved from Whangaparāoa.

name: Northland
boundary_note: Due to Northland being over quota we proposed moving a rural area between Whangaruru Harbour and Whananaki from Northland to Whangārei.

name: Ōtāhuhu
boundary_note: There are relatively significant changes to Ōtāhuhu, which shifts south-eastwards and is renamed from Panmure-Ōtāhuhu.

name: Pakuranga
boundary_note: Papakura moves southwards and shifts rural population to Botany, which in turn shifts some urban population to Pakuranga.

name: Palmerston North
boundary_note: Palmerston North expands around the city including the township of Bunnythorpe.

name: Papakura
boundary_note: Papakura moves southwards and shifts rural population to Botany, which in turn shifts some urban population to Pakuranga.

name: Port Waikato
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.

name: Rangitata
boundary_note: All these electorates remain unchanged from their 2020 boundaries and names.

name: Rangitīkei
boundary_note: Rangitīkei extends southwards to include Foxton, Levin and Manakau.

name: Remutaka
boundary_note: Hutt South and Remutaka both shift south-westwards, with the former taking in eastern Newlands.

name: Rotorua
boundary_note: Tauranga expands westward to the boundary with Coromandel; Bay of Plenty, which is renamed Mt Maunganui, gains the town centre and natural feature of the same name; and Rotorua expands northwards as far as the southern outskirts of Tauranga city.

name: Selwyn
boundary_note: Due to rapid growth in Selwyn, which was originally 14% over quota, we proposed moving the communities of Prebbleton and Templeton and their surrounding areas from Selwyn into Wigram.

name: Southland
boundary_note: Our proposed changes involved a population of around 900 in the vicinity of Nightcaps and Otautau moving from Southland to Invercargill.

name: Taieri
boundary_note: All these electorates remain unchanged from their 2020 boundaries and names.

name: Takanini
boundary_note: Substantial population is shifted from this electorate to Botany, Papakura and Ōtāhuhu.

name: Tāmaki
boundary_note: The boundaries of Auckland Central, Mt Albert and Epsom move in a roughly anticlockwise direction, while Tāmaki and Maungakiekie move eastwards and Mt Roskill moves westwards.

name: Taranaki-King Country
boundary_note: Taranaki-King Country gains Taumarunui.

name: Taupō
boundary_note: The boundaries of 49 general and three Māori electorates have been adjusted.

name: Tauranga
boundary_note: Tauranga expands westward to the boundary with Coromandel; Bay of Plenty, which is renamed Mt Maunganui, gains the town centre and natural feature of the same name; and Rotorua expands northwards as far as the southern outskirts of Tauranga city.

name: Tukituki
boundary_note: Instead, Napier gains a rural area from Tukituki north of the Ngaruroro River.

name: Upper Harbour
boundary_note: East Coast Bays also shifts small areas to both Upper Harbour and North Shore.

name: Waikato
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.

name: Waimakariri
boundary_note: All these electorates remain unchanged from their 2020 boundaries and names.

name: Wairarapa
boundary_note: Wairarapa incorporates Ashhurst.

name: Waitākere
boundary_note: New Lynn and parts of Kelston become Waitākere.

name: Waitaki
boundary_note: All these electorates remain unchanged from their 2020 boundaries and names.

name: Wellington Bays
boundary_note: Rongotai becomes Wellington Bays.

name: Wellington North
boundary_note: Wellington Central becomes Wellington North.

name: West Coast-Tasman
boundary_note: The Commission did receive a small number of submissions from West Coast-Tasman and Kaikōura, however we have been unable to accommodate these suggestions due to population quota requirements, and they remain unchanged from 2020 boundaries and names.

name: Whanganui
boundary_note: Whanganui extends north and north-eastwards incorporating Ōwhango and Waiouru.

name: Whangaparāoa
boundary_note: Kaipara ki Mahurangi shifts population to Upper Harbour and Henderson, while gaining an area from Whangaparāoa, which in turn shifts population to East Coast Bays.

name: Whangārei
boundary_note: Due to Northland being over quota we proposed moving a rural area between Whangaruru Harbour and Whananaki from Northland to Whangārei.

name: Wigram
boundary_note: Due to rapid growth in Selwyn, which was originally 14% over quota, we proposed moving the communities of Prebbleton and Templeton and their surrounding areas from Selwyn into Wigram.

name: Hauraki-Waikato
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.

name: Ikaroa-Rāwhiti
boundary_note: Ikaroa-Rāwhiti gains an area in Lower Hutt and its eastern bays area from Te Tai Tonga.

name: Tāmaki Makaurau
boundary_note: Accordingly, no changes have been made to this electorate as it remains within the required population quota.

name: Te Tai Hauāuru
boundary_note: The boundary between Te Tai Tonga and Te Tai Hauāuru has a minor adjustment in Horokiwi, affecting no population.

name: Te Tai Tokerau
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.

name: Te Tai Tonga
boundary_note: Ikaroa-Rāwhiti gains an area in Lower Hutt and its eastern bays area from Te Tai Tonga.

name: Waiariki
boundary_note: Nineteen electorates are unchanged.
